A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same See-NeRF work and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E. Existing content can be matched despite table renumbering and appendix reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original HDR, novel-exposure, and deblurring novel-view synthesis experiments, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and robustness analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds an EvHDR-GS comparison and an imaging-model ablation in Appendix D.4, Table 9.

M1.justification: The proposed radiance representation, RGB and event mapping fields, losses, and inference procedure are unchanged. See-NeRF# is an added experimental ablation, not a revision of the proposed method. The E2NeRF pose strategy discussed in new Appendix D.5 was already documented in Appendix C.2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain eight synthetic HDR scenes, five collected real scenes, and the Real-World-Challenge dataset for HDR, novel-exposure, and deblurring synthesis. The added comparison reports results for retained tasks; no new dataset or test population is introduced.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates EvHDR-GS against See-NeRF in Appendix D.4, Table 9. Existing comparison methods remain. Table 3 relabels the same Ev-DeblurNeRF-derived component from 'Simple Linear' to 'eCRF', with unchanged results, rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Table 9 adds an experimental control, See-NeRF#, that omits exposure integration and substitutes F(x)=x^a for the learned RGB CRF while retaining event-nonideality modeling. Previously reported data splits, metrics, training budgets, and pose settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.4 tests whether adopting EvHDR-GS's imaging model degrades See-NeRF, adding evidence about the combined importance of exposure integration and flexible RGB response modeling. Existing component ablations, noise/exposure robustness tests, hyperparameter analyses, and 3DGS experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and scene averages without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added comparison follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports HDR/deblurring PSNR values of 18.94/28.69 for EvHDR-GS and 19.75/28.35 for See-NeRF#. The full See-NeRF values of 26.49/32.70 repeat existing results. Numerical entries in the pre-existing tables remain unchanged after matching v1 Tables 9-15 to v3 Tables 10-16.

T1.justification: The sensor models, mathematical reasoning, and numbered equations in Sections 3-4 and Appendices A-B are unchanged. The power-law expression in new Appendix D.4 specifies the comparison configuration rather than adding a theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about sensor-physics-grounded HDR/deblurring synthesis from single-exposure images and events. The additional comparison supports these claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly acknowledges EvHDR-GS's similar post-rendering CRF placement and attributes performance differences to integration, CRF modeling, and event nonidealities. Appendix D.5 adds a future direction combining event supervision with advanced pose estimation. Existing interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page statement that code and data are publicly available, together with a project-page URL; v1 lacks this access information. Existing hardware, iteration counts, sampling settings, and other Appendix C implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds five cited works, including EvHDR-GS, AE-NeRF, EventSplat, MoBluRF, and CRiM-GS. Appendices D.4-D.5 provide targeted comparisons with related imaging and pose-estimation approaches, while the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision adds short Appendix D.4-D.5 subsections, makes limited wording and terminology edits, and updates affiliations and contact information. The main narrative and overall section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 9, supplies higher-resolution versions of Figures 3 and 5, and locally reflows appendix content and references. All 14 existing figures are retained, and subsequent detailed-results tables are renumbered without substantive display redesign.

improvement.justification: The added EvHDR-GS comparison and imaging-model ablation strengthen empirical support and clarify the relationship to a relevant prior method. Code/data access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are incremental: the core method and existing results are unchanged, and the new ablation changes integration and CRF modeling jointly, limiting attribution to individual components.
